original_query_traces.query: What information should a good GitHub issue contain, including optional supporting material?

results.text:
Open source etiquette

Well-run projects contain a few standard files:

  File                           Purpose

   README.md                     what the project is, how to install and use it

   LICENSE                       what others may legally do with the code

   CONTRIBUTING.md               how to contribute: branch names, code style, PR rules

   .gitignore                    files Git should not track

Releases turn a tag (Unit 4) into a downloadable version with notes: Releases → Draft a
new release → choose tag        v1.0  .

Issues: tracking work

An issue is a discussion about one task: a bug, a feature request, a question. Every
issue gets a number (     #3 ).

   🍽Mr. Desai reports a bug

   Title: Cart total wrong when the same item is added twice Body: Steps: 1) add
   Samosa, 2) add Samosa again, 3) open cart. Expected ₹30, shows ₹15. Phone:
   Android, Chrome.

A good issue has:

a clear title that names the problem,

   steps to reproduce, expected vs actual result,

   screenshots or error messages if possible.

Then the team:

   adds labels (   bug  ,  enhancement     , good first issue       ),

   assigns someone,

   discusses in comments (Markdown works; mention people with                  @username    ).
